definitions.explanation: The authority or power to govern a country or region. Also used to refer to a specific administration or government in power.

examples.japanese: {政権|せいけん}が{交代|こうたい}した。
{現|げん}{政権|せいけん}は{経済|けいざい}{改革|かいかく}を{進|すす}めている。
examples.english: The current administration is pushing forward economic reforms.

examples.japanese: {野党|やとう}は{次|つぎ}の{選挙|せんきょ}で{政権|せいけん}を{奪|うば}い{返|かえ}そうとしている。
examples.english: The opposition party is trying to reclaim power in the next election.

notes:
USAGE:
A central term in political news and discourse. Can refer abstractly to political power itself or concretely to a specific administration (e.g., {安倍|あべ}{政権|せいけん}, the Abe administration). Frequently appears in news headlines.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {政権|せいけん}{交代|こうたい}: change of government
- {政権|せいけん}を{握|にぎ}る: to hold power, to be in power
- {政権|せいけん}を{取|と}る: to take power
- {現|げん}{政権|せいけん}: the current administration
- {連立|れんりつ}{政権|せいけん}: coalition government

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {政府|せいふ}: government (the institution/organization)
- {内閣|ないかく}: cabinet (the prime minister and ministers)
